title: Round 36 Maine-Massachusetts state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Maine and Massachusetts. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Mount Katahdin and Mount Greylock carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. The three batch-17 corridor rivers that seed here (Androscoggin, Saco, Merrimack), the Sebago Lake adjacent-ID pair, and the still-unseeded Connecticut main stem are recorded below.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. County/township records, census-designated places, historical records, harbor/channel records, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Mount Katahdin (579940) and Mount Greylock (607448), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the summit elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-18; this register is the frozen batch-18 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (text class Reservoir for Moosehead Lake, Sebago Lake, and Quabbin Reservoir), Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor (the Connecticut main stem, now corridor-only in four consecutive frames).
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

maine.title: Maine statewide frame (Maine-Massachusetts batch)
maine.frameNote: Maine-Massachusetts batch: the Augusta capital anchor is balanced with the per-ID Mount Katahdin high point (5,270 ft), Cadillac Mountain, Moosehead and Sebago lakes, and four river mouth records. identityDecisions.candidate: Sebago Lake FEATURE_ID 575155 (Lakes & Reservoirs) vs 575156 (Populated Place)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded the water record 575155. GNIS registers the lake and the lakeside community under adjacent FEATURE_IDs; the class is the discriminator, and the rejected community record is named here rather than silently dropped.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a shoreline or centroid.

identityDecisions.candidate: Adjacent-ID utility/harbor records at Provincetown (616640) and New Bedford Reservoir (613715)
identityDecisions.decision: Not seeded. Both are the immediate FEATURE_ID neighbours of seeded records (Provincetown 616639, New Bedford 613714); adjacency is recorded so the seeded identification does not rest on the ID sequence.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Sequential IDs are not identity evidence; class, county, and point decide.

identityDecisions.decision: Seeded the Middlesex County record (the Charles River city, point matches); the Worcester County namesake community is not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a municipal boundary.

identityDecisions.candidate: Connecticut River under states=MA (reservoir-only, fourth consecutive frame)
identityDecisions.decision: Corridor-only again. The MA screen returns only Connecticut River Reservoir impoundments, as under NH and VT (batch 17). The river has now been corridor-only in four frames (NH, VT, MA, and its Springfield reach); its Stream record is expected on the Connecticut screen in the next batch and will be seeded there if returned.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridor is not a channel centerline or state boundary.

identityDecisions.candidate: Androscoggin River 580918, Saco River 574648, Merrimack River 619363 (mouth records)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded on their Maine/Massachusetts mouth records after reservoir-only or empty screens under New Hampshire (batch 17). This closes the batch-17 corridor pattern on the same terms as the Mississippi (Minnesota to Louisiana) and Pearl (Mississippi to Louisiana) chains.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The stored points are GNIS primary points at the returned mouth counties, not centerlines.

knownLimitations: Maine and Massachusetts are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by official name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Mount Katahdin (5,270 feet) and Mount Greylock (3,491 feet) elevations cite USGS-published values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. The Maine rectangle reaches to the Canadian border at latitude 47.5 and the Massachusetts rectangle includes Cape Cod and offshore water; no boundary geometry is claimed.
